transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Lee Carter (Redwood CSM); Maya Lopez (AcmeTech Head of Search); Arjun Patel (AcmeTech CTO); Nina Gomez (AcmeTech Data Eng)

Summary (auto): Redwood hosted API demo for embeddings + rerank focused on search relevance. Walkthrough of Console routes, Optimize recommendations, demo of embed->ann->rerank pattern, and discussion of POC scope and security requirements.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick us off. um we'll keep this to ~40ish minutes and leave time for q&a, priya from our se team will walk through the demo and console and then lee will cover onboarding and next steps.
[00:18] Maya (AcmeTech): thanks jordan, ya quick context - we're rebuilding our site search, currently on OpenSearch, looking for improved relevance esp for merchandising and long-tail queries. we care about latency under 120ms p50 and costs can't explode.
[00:32] Jordan: perfect, that's exactly why we wanted to show embeddings + rerank, you can keep ANN for recall and then apply a lightweight reranker to reorder results by relevance without huge token spend.
[00:45] Priya (Redwood SE): i'll share my screen now, apologies if the deck is a little rough i have a short demo notebook as well. first slide - hosted api endpoints: embeddings, rerank, search patterns. we support several embeddings models, we also expose a dedicated rerank endpoint that takes top-k candidates plus the query and returns a score ordering.
[01:10] Arjun (AcmeTech): quick q - is rerank a separate model call or is it like a prompt to the text gen endpoint?
[01:18] Priya: good question - it's a specialized pairing: the rerank endpoint can run a smaller cross-encoder style model optimized for scoring, so it's lower token spend than running a full chat/generate call for each doc, and it's tuned for latency. sometimes transcription shows "cross encoder" as "cross-encorder" - ignore that.
[01:40] Nina (AcmeTech): what's the typical latency when using embed + ann + rerank for say top-50 -> rerank top-10?
[01:48] Priya: depends on model & region; for our hosted tier we see combined p50 ~90-150ms for small models and ~120-220ms for higher-quality rerank models. with concurrency and batching Optimize suggests a config to keep p95 under your 300ms requirement.
[02:10] Jordan: we also have caching for prefix and KV cache to shave cold-start costs, that often helps merchants with repeat queries.
[02:22] Maya: ok good. can you show the console and how we tune batching/quantization?
[02:30] Priya: sure briefly - console -> routes -> model profile. here you can change the embeddings model, the rerank model, and see throughput/latency estimates. Optimize tab gives recommended batch sizes and quantization suggestions per workload.
[02:50] [screen demo noise] Priya: i'm switching to a notebook where i show a quick pipeline: ingest sample product CSV -> call embeddings endpoint to vectorize -> index into your ANN provider (we have integrated connectors, or you can use your existing OpenSearch kNN) -> query -> call rerank endpoint with top-k candidates.
[03:20] Maya: do you ingest into your index or we keep everything in our infra?
[03:26] Jordan: hosted option stores embeddings as part of the route if you use our managed ANN, but many customers keep vectors in their own index (OpenSearch, Pinecone, etc) and call rerank in Redwood. that's a common hybrid pattern.
[03:45] Arjun: for regs, can you explain data residency and encryption? we have EU-only data for some SKUs.
[03:53] Priya: yes - hosted supports region pinning (we can provision routes in eu-west), plus encryption at rest with KMS, and we provide audit logs. i'll send our SOC2 and data residency notes after the call.
[04:12] [00:04:30] Maya: how does billing look if we run both embeddings and rerank at scale? costs add up fast, right?
[04:22] Jordan: correct, it's a function of number of vector calls and rerank calls - Optimize provides token-level and call-level cost breakdowns. for rerank we often recommend a two-stage approach: cheap recall with ANNs and narrower top-k then rerank only top-10, that reduces token spend. also model selection matters - smaller rerank models are cheaper and can meet quality for many ecomm catalogs.
[04:55] Priya: i'll show a sample cost calc in the notebook - for a 10k qps workload with top10 reranks we show how cost scales and where you can trade latency for cheaper model choices.
[05:15] [00:05:15] Nina: our current infra does synchronous calls in the request path; will we need to move to async to hit targets?
[05:22] Priya: not necessarily, lots of customers keep sync path with batching and cache; Optimize suggests batch sizes that keep latency within SLOs. if you need burst handling we have autoscaling policies on Dedicated, but hosted also has autoscale and burst options.
[05:43] Jordan: reminder, if your SLA requires guaranteed throughput and capacity isolation, Dedicated is an option - but for POC hosted is fastest.
[05:58] [00:05:58] Arjun: any limits on tokens or rate limiting that would block our peak events?
[06:05] Priya: we have configurable rate limits and quotas; for enterprise customers we can lift limits and set rate-card based contracts. we'll need to size based on your peak queries and model choices.
[06:25] Maya: ok let's walk through a concrete example on sample data.
[06:30] Priya: i have a small sample catalog - watch the notebook: ingest 3k items, call embeddings model x-small, index to OpenSearch kNN, query "waterproof hiking jacket blue" -> ann returns 50 docs -> rerank with model r-small returns reordered top10. i'll paste the request/response in chat after.
[07:05] [00:07:05] Priya: note: transcription may show model names slightly off, e.g., r-small -> r smal in the transcript.
[07:20] Jordan: customers often ask about quality: we recommend a short eval set of ~2000 queries and expected precision/k metrics. that becomes your POC success criteria.
[07:34] Maya: our success criteria would be improving MRR and clicks-to-conversion on search results for merchandising queries - we can quantify that in the POC.
[07:50] Nina: from an engineering perspective, what effort to integrate? data pipelines, auth, monitoring?
[07:58] Lee (Redwood CSM): typical POC integration is 1-2 engineers for a week - mostly ingestion script + tiny rerank call integration. we provide onboarding SDKs, example ingestion scripts, and a sample dashboard in Console so you can see token/cost breakdowns.
[08:22] [00:08:22] Arjun: can you demo the logs/tracing? we need ability to audit queries tied to user ids for debugging - privacy concerns as well.
[08:31] Priya: yes console has per-route logs and trace hooks; we can also push logs to your SIEM. we redact PII by default and support customer-managed keys.
[08:50] Maya: any prebuilt connectors to OpenSearch?
[08:55] Priya: yes we have a connector for OpenSearch and Pinecone; for OpenSearch it's a script that maps vector ids back to your doc ids and we show an example mapping.
[09:10] [00:09:10] Nina: in the POC can we try with our own embeddings model? we have a fine-tuned encoder.
[09:19] Priya: you can bring your vector representations - either compute them offline and index, or host the model in your infra and call Redwood for rerank. hosted pipeline expects vectors in the shape of our embeddings API but if you provide vectors we can accept them as long as dimensions match.
[09:39] Jordan: another common ask - client wants SSO and roles. we support SAML SSO and RBAC in Console.
[09:50] Arjun: great. what's the expected turnaround for security docs?
[09:56] Lee: we'll send SOC2 + network diagrams and KMS integration details within 48 hours. priya will include a short benchmark spreadsheet.
[10:06] [00:10:06] Priya: switching back to Console: here you can create a route, pick embeddings model, pick rerank model, set batch and caching configs. Optimize suggests a batch size and whether to enable quantization (if on Dedicated or specific GPU profiles). you can also toggle "fallback model" to automatically route to cheaper model on congestion.
[10:35] Maya: fallback model sounds useful for Black Friday style spikes. does it preserve result consistency?
[10:41] Priya: yes we keep versioning and can do canary rollouts; fallback will use a model variant tested by Optimize for minimal quality regression. you can tie rollouts to eval sets.
[10:58] [00:10:58] Arjun: what about A/B testing between rerank models?
[11:03] Priya: Console supports per-route A/B split and compares quality metrics from your eval set and live signals.
[11:20] Maya: ok let's talk POC scope - what do you need from us?
[11:25] Jordan: ideally a sample dataset, expected query volume, and 1-2 priority metrics. we provided action items in chat: nina to share sample CSV, we will provision a trial route and api key for the POC.
[11:42] [00:11:42] Nina: timeline - we have a release window late october so we'd like a quick POC this week of the 18th.
[11:49] Jordan: we can do 10/18 start, run one week, and review results 10/25.
[11:57] Priya: i will prepare a short benchmark that shows p50/p95 for embed + ann + rerank on a 3k sample.
[12:10] Arjun: anything we should be wary of re: model hallucination when reranking?
[12:16] Priya: rerank models are discriminative so hallucination is far less likely than generation calls; main risk is model bias for certain query patterns, which we detect during evals.
[12:34] [00:12:34] Maya: can you share an example API request for rerank?
[12:39] Priya: yes i'll paste one in chat - basically calls rerank endpoint with query and list of candidate doc text or doc ids with embeddings. the response is a score array and new ordering.
[12:55] Jordan: ok i'm going to summarize next steps and then open to q's.
[13:00] [00:13:00] Jordan: recap: 1) Redwood to provision hosted trial route and api key; 2) Priya send security pack & benchmark spreadsheet; 3) Jordan send pricing worksheet; 4) AcmeTech to provide sample data + metrics; 5) target POC start 2026-10-18.
[13:25] Maya: sounds good - one more question: do you support per-customer rate limits and quotas per route?
[13:31] Lee: yes per-route quotas, token budgeting, and we can set alerts in Console.
[13:45] [00:13:45] Nina: thanks everyone, from our side we'll confirm dataset and internal stakeholders by Friday.
[13:53] Arjun: i might need the network diagram before we open firewall ports - appreciate the quick turn.
[14:00] Jordan: we'll get that over.
[14:06] [00:14:06] Maya: okay good demo, appreciate seeing the console and optimize tips.
[14:12] Jordan: thanks all. any final q's?
[14:18] [silence for a few sec]
[14:25] Jordan: cool we'll follow up in email with all artifacts, chat transcript includes the notebook and example requests. thanks for the time.
[14:32] Meeting ends.
